story: Gary is at home on a Monday afternoon, focused on securing his golf cart wiring with spare fuses and zip ties from his toolbox. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is determined to make Rosa's six o'clock supper, insisting she'll arrive with bells on and asking Rosa to pass along word to Gary about their doubles ladder match. Hal, dutifully keeping the committee's books, is tallying the pink flamingos visible from the street, while Rosa hopefully invites him to pot roast and tells him the count can wait.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Grab spare fuses and zip ties, then secure the cart wiring
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the total in my notebook for the committee

gary.thought_process: I've bench-tested and run the full cart test in the garage, and the wiring's solid. Last tick I was checking the toolbox for spare fuses and zip ties, so I should finish that: tidy the wiring so nothing rattles loose or shorts out. Everything stays inside the garage, out of street view, until Architectural Review approves under L-01. Then I can think about heading to Town Hall to check on the form.

parameters.content: Grab spare fuses and zip ties, then secure the cart wiring

donna.thought_process: Rosa just offered to build a dinner menu around my schedule, and I already told her six tonight, so I don't need to ask again. She's offering and I should confirm it warmly and tie it back to the ladder match. Hal is counting my flamingos for the committee, which is a little nerve-wracking, but I'll deal with that after. My real problem is Gary, who has gone missing before our first ladder match. Rosa's place is on this street, and I can ask her to pass word to Gary at dinner while keeping the plan clean. Better yet, I confirm six tonight with Rosa, then head off to find Gary at the rec center where the courts are.

parameters.content: Rosa, six tonight is perfect, no need to build around me, I'll be there with bells on. And if you spot Gary before I do, tell him his doubles partner is hunting for him, we have a ladder match to win!

hal.thought_process: Donna and Rosa are right here, and the flamingo flock is in front of me. My goal is to report the flock to the committee, and L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. My memory shows Donna already ordered a count, but I haven't done my own. A proper report needs a documented tally, and a supply sergeant keeps accurate inventory. I'll count first, with no accusations until I have a number. I'll keep it quiet, since Rosa's dinner invitation was warm and I don't want to spoil the mood.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and write the total in my notebook for the committee

rosa.thought_process: Donna confirmed six o'clock tonight, so she's locked in. She's asking where Gary is, and I haven't seen him, so no need to repeat my invite to her. Hal is standing right here and he's the one who's been drifting off and leaving my table waiting. He's counting flamingos for the committee, which is his usual thing. I invited him back at tick 1 and got no clear answer, so a short, warm, direct ask about tonight is the next step. Keep it blunt and kind, no guilt, and tie it to Donna's six o'clock so it's one dinner with a time.

parameters.content: Hal, Donna's coming at six tonight and I'm setting a place for you too. No pressure about the flamingo count, it'll still be here after pot roast. Can I count on you?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
